formal_entries.label: qu:i-good-no-bmp
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:i-good-no-bmp}
Extend the complete topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} to ordinary models of zero lower volume and beyond bounded mass, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Recover the curve topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} and the background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, including higher-dimensional limits that lose bigness or positive lower volume.

formal_entries.label: qu:nef-degeneration-exponent
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:nef-degeneration-exponent}
Which geometric conditions on a nonclosed nef background force a common degeneration order, or an integral one? When is equality attained in the modification and residual order comparisons?
formal_entries.state: Both orders lie in $[0,n]$ and are independent of $\mu$ and $h$, of positive scaling, and of smooth gauge. For closed nef backgrounds on a K\"ahler manifold they equal $n-\operatorname{nd}(\theta)$. Nonclosed examples on products of elliptic curves realize unequal orders, irrational common orders, and zero volume with decay slower than every positive power. A modification can strictly increase the orders; effective residual subtraction also gives a one-sided comparison. Explicit elliptic threefolds have integral orders determined by the rank of their boundary forms. The flat-torus criterion separates current rigidity from rank: a nonzero semipositive boundary class is rigid exactly when its kernel leaves are dense, equivalently when a fixed positive perturbation collapses in diameter (Book, Theorem~27.16.1, printed p.~958). Irrational and rational kernel slopes give the two alternatives (Book, Example~27.16.1, printed p.~959). Arbitrary approaching flat K\"ahler forms can collapse at a nonrigid limiting class (Book, Example~27.16.2, printed p.~959). These metric distinctions do not supply the nonclosed degeneration-order conditions asked for here. A Kummer resolution also has a nonzero smooth semipositive, nonrigid irrational boundary class with square zero (Book, Proposition~27.17.1, printed p.~961). A global periodic $\ddc$ primitive identifies the representatives' Bott--Chern classes, and two explicitly translated torus periods detect the irrational ray. The resolved surface contains sixteen exceptional curves (Book, Lemma~27.17.1, printed p.~960); the example does not address the curve-free regime of P11.\par Book, Lemma~25.17.3, printed p.~771 proves a full-Gauduchon-infimum comparison when $\theta\leq CB$ and $\theta+\ddc\varphi\geq cB$, with $\varphi\in L^1$, $c,C>0$, and $B$ closed semipositive on a compact K\"ahler manifold. Constant rank $R$ gives two-sided variational-volume bounds by $\epsilon^{n-R}$ for arbitrary smooth positive probability and Hermitian perturbation. Theorem~25.17.1, printed p.~773 constructs such a comparison for products of projective spaces and their linear-center blowups. The fixed cone has nonnegative parameters in $\theta=\sum_i((a_i+b_if_i)H_i+(c_i+d_ig_i)Q_i)$, with strictly positive fixed smooth $f_i,g_i$, omitted $Q_i$ terms on plain factors, and fixed pullback Fubini--Study generators. These functions may depend on every product coordinate. Each $H_i$-active block contributes $m_i$ to $R$, each $Q_i$-only blown block contributes $m_i-\ell_i-1$, and an inactive block contributes zero. All zero parameters and the zero background are included. An exceptional-divisor logarithm supplies the lower current bound; no restricted invariant/product test or Monge--Amp\`ere mass extremum replaces the variational infimum.\par Proposition~25.17.10, printed p.~774 preserves this order under every specified product linear blowup and, more generally, every modification with compact K\"ahler manifold source. In the latter case the book also proves two-sided power bounds, using the closed-background intersection polynomial after pulling back the actual nonzero divisor sections. The upstairs probability is independently smooth and positive; a degenerate pullback probability is not used in the smooth dual formula.\par Lemma~25.17.4, printed p.~775 determines the exact numerical range of the specified finite effective real sums of zero divisors of sections of integer tensor powers of the $H_i,Q_i$ bundles, with their fixed metrics: $\delta_i\geq0$ on plain factors and $\delta_i\geq0$, $\delta_i+\rho_i\geq0$ on blown factors. Theorem~25.17.2, printed p.~776 assumes the sufficient representation-preserving inequalities $a_i\geq\delta_i$, $c_i\geq\rho_i$. The residual remains in the same nef cone, its order gap is $\sum_i(R_i(\theta)-R_i(\beta))\geq0$, and equality holds exactly when every initially $H_i$-active block retains $a_i-\delta_i+b_i>0$ and every initially $Q_i$-only block retains $c_i-\rho_i+d_i>0$. Example~25.17.1, printed p.~776 gives genuinely nonclosed positive $\theta_t=tH+gQ$ and residual $(t-s)H+(g+s)Q$ after removal of $sE$, $0\leq s\leq t$. Equality holds for $s<t$, while $s=t$ gives jump $\ell+1$, realizing every integer from one to the dimension minus one. The chosen boundary current has actual divisorial mass, although perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities remain zero.\par Book, Proposition~25.17.11, printed p.~777 removes the constant-rank requirement in this comparison. For a smooth closed semipositive $B$, put $R=\max_X\operatorname{rank}B$. The full quotient comparison and closed intersection polynomial give the same two-sided $\epsilon^{n-R}$ bounds: $B^{R+1}=0$, and the top nonzero mixed coefficient is positive on a nonempty open set. The target background is still nef, the ambient manifold is K\"ahler, and the lower comparison still requires its global $L^1$ potential. Corollary~25.17.2, printed p.~778 applies to any finite collection of smooth closed semipositive generators $B_j$ with fixed strictly positive smooth $f_j$ and parameters $t_j\geq0$: $\theta=\sum_jt_jf_jB_j$. Its order is $n-\max_X\operatorname{rank}(\sum_{t_j>0}B_j)$, including the empty active set. It preserves this order and the power bounds under every modification with compact K\"ahler manifold source, using only smooth pulled-back comparisons. The actual rank of the sum accounts for overlapping generators; constants are not asserted uniform across parameter faces. Example~25.17.2, printed p.~778 gives nonclosed $(f\circ p_2)p_1^*(b\omega_1)$ on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^q$, with $f>0$ nonconstant, $b\geq0$ nonzero and zero on an open set, and exact order $q$. Thus the closed generators themselves may have open zero-rank regions.\par A smooth compact connected anticanonical curve $D$ with $D^2=0$ in a complex surface has a unitary flat divisor line on a neighborhood (Book, Theorem~25.17.3, printed p.~781). The complete local proof uses a holonomy-independent flat elliptic inverse and a weighted fiberwise contraction; no arithmetic condition on the degree-zero normal line is imposed. A concave logarithmic cutoff gives a smooth closed semipositive divisor curvature $B$, supported in an annulus, of rank at most one (Book, Proposition~25.17.12, printed p.~783). On a compact K"ahler surface its maximum rank is exactly one, because $\int_SB\wedge\kappa=\int_D\kappa>0$. Every fixed smooth $f>0$ therefore gives a nef background $fB$ with two-sided variational-volume bounds by $\epsilon$ for arbitrary Hermitian perturbation and smooth positive probability; choices with $\mathrm df\wedge B\ne0$ are nonclosed (Book, Corollary~25.17.3, printed p.~784). For the closed perturbation, $\mathcal V_\mu(B+\epsilon\kappa)=2\epsilon\int_D\kappa+\epsilon^2\int_S\kappa^2$. Nine successive blowups along the strict transforms of a smooth plane cubic, including infinitely near centers, give these anticanonical square-zero curves (Book, Proposition~25.17.13, printed p.~784). The anticanonical line is semiample exactly when its elliptic normal line is torsion; exact order $m$ gives the first moving, basepoint-free system $|mD|$. For a non-torsion normal line every $|kD|$ is the singleton $\{kD\}$, yet the smooth rank-one semipositive curvature and nonclosed order-one multiples still exist. Thus the comparison class includes geometric generators that have no generated positive tensor power.\par The flat neighborhood also controls the divisor complement. For a smooth compact connected divisor in a complex manifold of dimension at least two, a flat divisor line gives compact Levi-flat circle levels. A torsion normal line of exact order $m$ gives a proper local holomorphic function with divisor $mD$ and connected compact nonzero fibers (Book, Proposition~25.17.14, printed p.~786). A non-torsion normal line has dense Levi leaves; maximum modulus forces every holomorphic function on a punctured tube to be constant. Thus every compact-hole complement that is connected has only constant holomorphic functions, which extend to the full divisor complement (Book, Theorem~25.17.4, printed p.~786). For either holonomy regime the complement is not Stein; in particular the non-torsion nine-point cubic example has the Hartogs property and only constant global holomorphic functions (Book, Corollary~25.17.4, printed p.~787). These complement results retain the flat-neighborhood hypothesis and do not supply a comparator for a general nonclosed nef background.
formal_entries.gap: No unrestricted common-order or integrality assertion survives the examples. Find hypotheses on geometry, torsion, or the degenerating positive representatives that force the closed-type behavior, and characterize equality in the comparison inequalities. These results fix strictly positive coefficient functions and specified closed semipositive generators or global current comparisons. Their divisor inequalities are sufficient for the displayed residual representation and do not characterize every nef residual or alternative cone representation. Fixed functions that vanish and modifications with non-Kahler source remain outside the proved regime. The maximum-rank criterion also requires a closed semipositive comparator and its stated global current comparison. It does not classify backgrounds without such a comparator or arbitrary vanishing coefficient functions. The generator corollary pulls back only smooth comparisons, so it makes no assertion about pulling back a general $L^1$ potential. The flat-divisor construction adds a geometric family within this comparison criterion; it does not provide a comparator for an arbitrary nonclosed nef background or classify all compact complex surfaces.

formal_entries.label: conj:lck-lee-psef
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:lck-lee-psef}
For every compact strictly LCK manifold, the ordinary Bott--Chern class $\{\kappa_\lambda\}$ is pseudoeffective.

formal_entries.label: q:lck-gauduchon-volume
formal_entries.text:
\label{q:lck-gauduchon-volume}
Does a compact LCK manifold have at most one Gauduchon LCK metric with a specified Lee class, specified twisted Bott--Chern class and specified smooth positive volume form?

formal_entries.label: conj:lck-calabi-yau-vaisman
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:lck-calabi-yau-vaisman}
A compact complex manifold with $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}(X)=0$ that admits a strictly LCK metric admits a Vaisman metric.

formal_entries.label: qu:hermitian-i-characterization
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-i-characterization}
For a big nonclosed background on a manifold with bounded mass, find criteria for $\underline{\operatorname{vol}}_\theta(P_\theta[u]_{\mathcal I})>0$ in terms of restricted multiplier ideals or divisorial orders. When this lower volume vanishes, which implications between envelope equality and upper-volume equality in \cref{prop:conditional-i-characterization} remain valid?

formal_entries.label: qu:individual-equation-threshold
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:individual-equation-threshold}\index{Subsolution!exact threshold equation problem}
Suppose $v_-(h)=0$. For a nonzero $0\leq f\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ with $b_h(f)>0$, does there exist $u\in\PSH(X,h)$ such that
\[
 \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_h(u)=b_h(f)f\,\mathrm{d}V?
\]
Determine the singularity or envelope class in which such an equation should be posed.

formal_entries.label: conj:nef-gaud-volume-big
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:nef-gaud-volume-big}\index{Gauduchon variational volume!bigness conjecture}
Let $\theta$ be a nef smooth real $(1,1)$-background on a compact complex manifold. Then
\[
 \mathcal V_\mu(\theta)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \theta\text{ is big}.
\]
Here $\mu$ is any smooth strictly positive probability measure.

formal_entries.label: qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge}
Let $\alpha$ be closed and nef with $\int_X\alpha^n>0$. Prove a positive lower bound for $\lambda_\mu(\alpha)$, and rule out the collapse in \cref{prop:gaud-positive-volume-collapse} for a sequence minimizing the bigness threshold of $\alpha$.

formal_entries.label: qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint}
Find geometric conditions beyond the metric identities in \cref{cor:geometric-determinant-bound} that imply the endpoint estimate in \eqref{eq:pvp-endpoint-geometric}, and identify how they exclude the lower-mass degeneration of \cref{sec:vanishing-lower-mass}.
formal_entries.state:
The manuscript proves the exact equivalence
\[v_-(h)>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \sup_{T\in\mathscr G_h}\|k_T\|_{L^{n/(n-1)}(\mathrm dV)}<\infty,\quad
 \sup\|k_T\|_{n/(n-1)}=v_-(h)^{-1/n}.\]
Every strictly smaller exponent is uniformly controlled on arbitrary compact complex manifolds. The endpoint holds if a metric's first two powers are $\ddc$-closed, including K\"ahler manifolds and compact complex surfaces. A balanced BMP threefold has zero lower mass and violates the endpoint even for smooth positive tests. Theorem~25.14.1, printed p.~742, gives a geometric sufficient condition for principal elliptic threefolds over K\"ahler surfaces: the sum of the squares of the real curvature forms is nonnegative and nonzero. The bounded cubic identity gives the exact positive lower mass of the split metric and the endpoint for the full normalized current family in every Hermitian background. These manifolds have no pluriclosed metric. Proposition~25.14.2, printed p.~743, constructs negative-line-bundle quotients with nonzero second real cohomology; Proposition~25.14.3, printed p.~744, constructs a Calabi--Eckmann family without LCK metrics. Proposition~25.14.1, printed p.~742, identifies the opposite sign for primitive curvature pairs.
formal_entries.gap: The nonnegative curvature-pair criterion settles the stated principal elliptic threefold families. Find further geometric conditions, including changing-sign curvature, primitive elliptic bundles and higher-dimensional geometries. Balancedness plus BMP is insufficient. A bounded determinant density for one smooth maximizer gives no bound for all tests or all near-maximizing sequences.

formal_entries.label: prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass
formal_entries.text:
\label{prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass}
Determine the lower Monge--Amp\`ere mass of the primitive elliptic bundles
above, in particular those of \cref{ex:primitive-elliptic-k3}.
Does it vanish whenever the real Chern class is nonzero?

formal_entries.label: qu:chern-ricci-gaud-singularities
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:chern-ricci-gaud-singularities}
Suppose a Chern--Ricci flow has finite maximal time $\tau$ and $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta_\tau)>0$. Can one prove that $\theta_\tau$ is big and that the flow converges smoothly to a positive metric locally on $X\setminus E_{\mathrm{nH}}(\theta_\tau)$, without a bounded mass hypothesis? How do the annihilating Gauduchon currents describe the resulting degeneracy?

formal_entries.label: qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program}
Use the coexistence of a balanced metric and a pluriclosed metric to construct closed positive data, or to control a geometric flow that can change the torsion. Determine what estimate beyond the finite balanced trace prevents metric degeneration. Can determinant estimates for Gauduchon currents contribute to that estimate?

formal_entries.label: qu:hermitian-morse-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-morse-program}
Find geometric hypotheses controlling the cost in \eqref{eq:gaud-volume-subtraction-cost} up to a nef endpoint beyond the closed-core regime of \cref{thm:closed-core-subtraction}. Determine when positive root volume forces bigness without that core. For closed backgrounds, compare the estimate with classical Morse inequalities; for nonclosed backgrounds, retain the differential data and the dependence on $\mu$.

formal_entries.label: qu:gaud-metric-boundary
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:gaud-metric-boundary}
For a specified finite-dimensional cone of smooth background classes, describe the metric completion of its unit-volume hypersurface. Which boundary points admit a current representative, and what estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguish finite from infinite distance?
formal_entries.status: partially resolved for invariant background cones; general question open
formal_entries.state: Homogeneity gives an isometry $(\mathscr C,g)\simeq(\mathbb R\times\mathscr S,\mathrm dr^2+g_{\mathscr S})$ with $r=\log\lambda$. Thus paths with volume tending to zero or infinity have infinite length. The product cone on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ is complete; the blowup of $\mathbb P^2$ has a finite-distance positive-nef-volume boundary. For a compact complex Lie-group quotient, a normalized invariant probability and a fixed real linear subspace $W\subset\operatorname{Herm}(n)$ containing a positive matrix, Book, Theorem~25.5.1, printed p.~693 proves that $\mathscr S=\{A>0:H\det A=1\}$ is complete and proper. Its Cauchy sequences are exactly coefficient sequences converging to a positive matrix. Book, Proposition~25.5.2, printed p.~690 identifies the normalized minimizing form as $\gamma_A=\theta_A/(H\det A)^{1/n}$ and characterizes positive-current coefficient classes by $A\geq0$. Spectral bounds control $\gamma_A$ pointwise. A nonzero singular coefficient limit becomes infinitely distant after normalization. In the full Iwasawa cone, Book, Example~25.5.2, printed p.~695 gives the exact logarithmic matrix distance and the explicit rate $\sqrt2|\log\varepsilon|/3$ for $\operatorname{diag}(1,1,\varepsilon)$ after normalization. Book, Theorem~25.5.2, printed p.~698 extends the determinant formula and the same complete prescribed coefficient metric on the Iwasawa quotient to every smooth probability invariant along its central elliptic fibers. These are exactly the smooth probabilities maximizing the volume of each invariant positive background. The minimizing metric is obtained from a closed base equation for the Schur complement; its coefficient mean retains the spectral distance bounds, without a claimed pointwise order estimate for the varying form. Book, Proposition~25.5.3, printed p.~696 identifies the upper mass of every invariant threefold positive background as $H\det A$. Book, Corollary~25.5.1, printed p.~697 gives zero non-pluripolar top mass for all plurisubharmonic potentials of singular semipositive invariant coefficients in dimension three.
formal_entries.gap: Classify the unit-volume completion for other specified background cones and reference densities, together with their current representatives and minimizing-metric estimates. The general Lie-group result uses the invariant probability, while the larger fiber-invariant density family is proved specifically on the Iwasawa quotient. Densities varying along its central fibers have strictly smaller variational volume; their Hessian completion is not determined by that value inequality. Nonzero singular coefficient limits in the proved matrix families are infinitely distant after normalization, while a raw sequence tending to zero may normalize to an existing positive point. Adjoining all nef classes does not give the answer. Distances may shorten after enlarging the cone; no infinite-dimensional completion follows.

formal_entries.label: conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint}\index{Adjoint measure!continuous-density conjecture}
For a Hermitian background $\omega$, the nonsingular reference $\varphi=0$, and every real $F\in C(X)$, the set $\mathcal A_0(F)$ consists of a single probability measure.

formal_entries.label: qu:singularity-topology-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:singularity-topology-program}\index{Singularity type!topology problem}
Extend the complete metrizable topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} on ordinary models beyond bounded mass and positive lower volume, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Preserve the smooth-gauge and two-sided background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, and treat background limits losing bigness or a uniform positive lower-volume bound. Recover the complete polar-variation topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} on all curve models, and determine whether the higher-dimensional extension is completely metrizable.

formal_entries.label: qu:exact-trace-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:exact-trace-program}
If $Y$ fails at least one of the two mass properties, can the Hermitian background $\Omega$ in \cref{thm:trace-profile-model-envelope} be chosen so that
\[
 \nu\bigl(\mathcal T_\Omega(u;Y)\circ\pi,E\bigr)
       =\tau_{Y,u}(E)
\]
for every prime divisor $E$ on every smooth modification $\pi$ of $Y$? If so, determine a background-compatible ordinary or ideal singularity class of this realization, and prove its addition and approximation properties.

formal_entries.label: qu:positive-system-recovery
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:positive-system-recovery}
For a smooth big background on a manifold without bounded mass, find a condition on a compatible Hermitian envelope system that forces recovery of its ideal type at every finite parameter. It should recover the positive limiting lower-volume criterion of \cref{thm:positive-volume-system-recovery} when bounded mass holds. Specify the invariant and uniform estimates that replace the finite upper-volume deficit, and their behavior under modifications.

formal_entries.label: qu:partial-kernel-lower-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:partial-kernel-lower-program}
Identify hypotheses on a weighted section series and its intrinsic growth dimension under which the partial Fubini--Study potentials attain the envelope lower bound and the normalized kernel measures converge. Relate the limiting measure to the Hermitian background while retaining the closed curvature and the growth dimension of the series.
formal_entries.state: The general upper-envelope bound is proved. A matching lower bound and kernel-measure convergence hold in the closed-curvature positive-mass setting with a K\"ahler modification, retaining its Jacobian and relative canonical bundle. Descended series on submersions give base-dimensional limits. Isolated-point conditions permit finite-codimension comparison; horizontal projective and explicit Hopf series give further exact limits. Hopf growth has degree $n-1$, so normalization by $m^n$ would discard its nonzero limit. An interior rational Newton polytope on a product of projective lines gives a complete sufficient-condition model when its affine hull has an integral offset, its smooth invariant logarithmic weight is strictly convex, and its sampling probability is smooth, strictly positive and invariant on the whole manifold. Book, Theorem~26.16.1, printed p.~887 proves the specified growth-envelope lower bound, all finite $L^p$ convergence and weighted Bernstein--Markov. Book, Theorem~26.16.2, printed p.~889 computes the positive relative-dimensional kernel limit as lattice volume lifted to real moment tori. It is independent of the invariant sampling probability. In lower dimension it is singular and differs from the ambient mixed envelope-curvature measure; in full dimension it equals the non-pluripolar top product. Book, Example~26.16.1, printed p.~890 includes nonclosed smooth sampling and a rational map with indeterminacy. A critical divisor multiplier-ideal family on a product of projective lines has positive growth exponent $q$ and potentials converging to its actual ideal envelope, while its $q!m^{-q}$-normalized kernel measures have two different positive weak limits. Book, Theorem~26.17.1, printed p.~891 computes $N_m=a_m(m+1)^q$, with $a_m=1$ in even and $2$ in odd degrees, and restores a single probability limit after division by $N_m$. Its selector has zero top non-pluripolar mass and its ideal family is not multiplicative. This shows that a growth exponent alone is insufficient outside the positive-mass convergence regime.\par An actual ideal selector at the two isolated base points of a pencil on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ gives a convergent non-multiplicative model. Book, Lemma~26.18.1, printed p.~894 identifies its all-weight ideal and ordinary upper type classes for every genuine competitor. Theorem~26.18.1, printed p.~896 computes the full ideal envelope for the specified compact logarithmic box and quadratic norm weight. Proposition~26.18.1, printed p.~897 gives the entire three-band space and exact dimension $3m+1$. Theorem~26.18.2, printed p.~898 proves a global potential lower bound, every finite $L^p$ convergence, uniform exponential convergence and an intrinsic positive measure limit of mass three. Additive error remains unbounded near each pole at every fixed degree $m\geq2$. The norm, box and sampling probability are fixed; this selector also has zero top non-pluripolar mass.
formal_entries.gap: Find intrinsic hypotheses producing enough sections with the full ideal constraints and controlling their measures. The Newton theorem specifies a growth-constrained target; it does not identify an arbitrary multiplier-ideal envelope. Boundary-touching polytopes, noninvariant data and general selected series remain outside its hypotheses. Preserve closed line-bundle curvature while relating the limit to a possibly nonclosed ambient background. No unqualified equality with the raw Hermitian Monge--Amp\`ere measure of the selecting weight follows from the upper bound. Require convergence of the normalized section counts for a finite weak kernel-measure limit, rather than merely an intrinsic growth exponent. The specific three-band pencil model does not establish a universal all-weight ideal/ordinary class identity or convergence for other compact sampling and arbitrary selected families.

formal_entries.label: qu:fiber-selected-approximation
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:fiber-selected-approximation}
Let $\pi:X\to B$ be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected compact complex manifolds with connected fibers, where $B$ is K\"ahler of dimension $q\geq1$. Fix a Hermitian form $\omega$ on $X$, a holomorphic line bundle $A$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $B$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(X,\omega)$. Set $\theta=c_1(A,h)$. For positive integers $m$, identify
\[
 V_m=H^0\bigl(X,\pi^*A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\varphi)\bigr)
          \subseteq H^0(B,A^m)
\]
by holomorphic descent. Find geometric or analytic conditions that produce $\psi\in\PSH(B,\theta)$ of positive non-pluripolar mass such that, for all sufficiently large $m$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 W_m=H^0\bigl(B,A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\psi)\bigr)\subseteq V_m,\\
 \dim V_m-\dim W_m=o(m^q).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Determine which features of the singularities of $\varphi$ along the fibers suffice for this approximation.

formal_entries.label: prob:growing-jets-localization
formal_entries.text:
\label{prob:growing-jets-localization}
Let $C$ be a connected compact Riemann surface, let $x\in C$, and let $(L,h)$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle whose curvature is semipositive and strictly positive on $C\setminus\{x\}$. Fix an integer $r\geq1$. Suppose that in a local coordinate $z$ centered at $x$ and a holomorphic frame $e$ one has
\[
 |e|_h^2=\mathrm{e}^{-\phi},\qquad
 \phi(z)=|z|^{2r}+O(|z|^{2r+1}).
\]
Let $\nu$ be a smooth positive volume form with local expression $a(z)\,\mathrm{d}A$ and $a(0)=1$, where $\mathrm{d}A$ is Euclidean area. For positive integers $m$, choose integers $q_m\to\infty$ with $q_m=o(m)$. Give
\[
 V_m=H^0(C,L^m\otimes\mathfrak m_x^{q_m})
\]
the norm $\|s\|^2=\int_C|s|_{h^m}^2\,\mathrm{d}\nu$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the ideal sheaf of $x$. Write $B_m=\sum_j|s_{m,j}|_{h^m}^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(s_{m,j})$ of $V_m$, with value zero when $V_m=0$. Determine the growth ranges of $q_m$ for which, for each fixed real $\tau$, every sequence of points $x_m$ in the coordinate neighborhood satisfying
\[
 m|z(x_m)|^{2r}=q_m/r+\tau\sqrt{q_m/r}
\]
obeys
\[
 \frac{\pi B_m(x_m)}{mr^2|z(x_m)|^{2r-2}}
 \longrightarrow
 \Phi(\tau):=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}
                         \mathrm{e}^{-s^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}s.
\]
When this transition law fails, determine how further terms of the local weight change its center and scale.

formal_entries.label: qu:singular-space-equations-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:singular-space-equations-program}
Beyond the projective-cone constructions of \cref{sec:projective-cone-equations}, determine geometric and measure conditions on compact unibranch Hermitian spaces that give existence and uniqueness in specified singularity classes. Identify estimates ensuring finite mass, descent and continuity, and their behavior under common refinements.
formal_entries.state:
The appendix proves disk-test descent under modifications and compatibility of ordinary envelopes, constructs resolution-independent non-pluripolar products, and gives explicit equations on projective cones under stated inequalities on their data. Dang provides continuity for bounded solutions under additional hypotheses, notably a log-terminal setting. Pan constructs a Gauduchon metric on the regular locus uniformly comparable to the prescribed metric, with conformal uniqueness up to scale.
 In the explicitly assumed standard nodal small-resolution model, Book, Lemma~13.18.3 constructs a strict analytic barrier and Corollary~13.18.1 gives a bounded fixed-smooth-density equation by subsequential potential degeneration, with exact exceptional-area decay. Book, Lemma~13.18.4 computes the pushed-forward density: it is in $L^p$ precisely for $1\leq p<3$, has a weak $L^3$ endpoint and is not in $L^3$ when a node is present. The bounded potential descends, including for a nonclosed ambient background, and solves (Book, equation~13.52) on the singular space. When the pullback background is closed, Book, Theorem~13.18.2 proves uniqueness among bounded normalized solutions and convergence of the entire smooth perturbation family. These arguments do not establish continuity at a node or settle the general prescribed-class problem.\par For compact unibranch curves with finite bijective torus normalization, Book, Lemma~A.7.1, printed p.~1178 constructs a periodic Green function directly. Theorem~A.7.1, printed p.~1179 proves an equation in every prescribed finite logarithmic ordinary type of total pole weight $A<H$, for nonzero nonnegative normalization-side $L^p$ data with $p>1$. Here $H=\int_E\pi^*h$, $\beta_0$ is flat area probability on the normalization $E$, and $f\geq0$ is its data density. The proportionality constant is $(H-A)/\int f\beta_0$, the entire genuine type has mass $H-A$, and uniqueness includes initially rough competitors. Disk lifts give genuine descent, a continuous residual and extended-value continuity at the poles; all curve resolutions and refinements are biholomorphic to the normalization. The local-embedding background may pull back degenerately. Example~A.7.1, printed p.~1181 supplies a nonnormal projective cusp with genus-one normalization, background mass six and a weight-one pole of nonpluripolar mass five. Its normalization-side density is smooth and positive, but the downstairs density belongs to $L^r(h)$ exactly for $1\leq r<2$, with logarithmic divergence at $r=2$. This is a dimension-one sufficient condition; all curve backgrounds are closed.\par Book, Theorem~A.7.2, printed p.~1184 gives an exact endpoint for normalization-side densities with local form $C_0|z|^{-2}(\log(1/|z|))^{-\gamma}$, where $C_0>0$ and the density is smoothly and positively extended away from the chosen point. They are integrable exactly for $\gamma>1$ and lie outside every $L^p$, $p>1$. Within this family, a positive-proportionality equation has a solution in the prescribed ordinary logarithmic type exactly for $\gamma>2$; it is unique in that entire type and has a continuous residual with no positive H\"older exponent upstairs. For $1<\gamma\leq2$, a constructed genuine descended solution has the same mass $H-A$ and all-weight resolution multiplier ideals, but its residual is unbounded below. No ordinary-type solution exists, even with an unspecified positive proportionality constant. The proof uses a cutoff radial primitive and a smooth mean-zero Green correction; it retains the possibly degenerate background.\par In every dimension $n\geq2$, an explicit product of a cuspidal curve with square elliptic curves has a nonclosed local-embedding Hermitian background whose normalization admits a positive smooth reference repair and has all background powers $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm c}$-closed (Book, Proposition~A.8.1, printed p.~1186). Fix an integer $s\geq n+3$ before choosing its sufficiently small nonzero real perturbation. A quantitative contraction solves full-variable normalized densities in a small $H^s$ neighborhood of the positive reference density, with a $C^2$ normalization-side potential and solution form at least one quarter of the flat reference (Book, Theorem~A.8.1, printed p.~1187). Every bounded ordinary potential has the same mass, and a weighted decreasing-product limit gives uniqueness against all bounded competitors, including rough ones (Book, Lemma~A.8.1, printed p.~1188; Proposition~A.8.2, printed p.~1188). The normalized potential descends genuinely, is ambient H\"older of exponent $1/3$, has forced scalar $c=M/\nu(X)$, and solves the equation on every resolution and common refinement. The datum gives the cusp locus zero mass; near it the exact downstairs density is $\lambda f/\rho$, with $\rho=4|z|^2+9|z|^4$ (Book, Theorem~A.8.2, printed p.~1189). Separately, the existing bounded-mass theorem on the positive repaired normalization gives bounded existence for every nonzero nonnegative normalization-side $L^p$ density, $p>1$, without the smallness condition (Book, Corollary~A.8.1, printed p.~1191). Regularity and entire bounded-class uniqueness are established here for the small Sobolev regime. The original general problem remains open.
formal_entries.gap: Find assumptions giving finite mass, existence, uniqueness in the specified class, and continuity downstairs, stable under common refinements. Arbitrary unibranch singularities are not covered by log-terminal results. Scalar bounds and resolution-level regularity do not alone supply descent or control near the singular locus. Torus normalization, finitely many logarithmic poles and normalization-side integrability are fixed hypotheses. The curve theorem gives no criterion for arbitrary singularity types or higher-dimensional nonclosed backgrounds. A criterion for arbitrary integrable normalization-side data remains open. The explicit endpoint construction does not prove a mass or uniqueness theorem for the whole resolution-ideal class.

supplemental_entries.title: Support and pluripolarity of excess-mass defect measures
supplemental_entries.statement:
For the smooth admissible sequence in \bk{cor:smooth-capacity-mass-defect}, $w_j\to0$ in capacity, the masses equal a prescribed $b>\int_X\omega^n$, and a subsequence satisfies
\[(\omega+\ddc w_j)^n\rightharpoonup\omega^n+\sigma,\qquad
 \sigma(X)=b-\int_X\omega^n.\]
Determine which supports and pluripolar charging behaviors are possible for these defect measures.
supplemental_entries.state: The shallow truncation regions converge in total variation to $\omega^n$; every fixed deep-tail restriction has weak limit $\sigma$. The currents converge in coefficient $L^1$ and their Gauduchon traces in total variation. These strong linear convergences do not remove the nonlinear defect. A separate local example shows that smooth bounded psh functions on any bounded domain in $\mathbb C^n$, $n\geq2$, can tend to zero in every finite $L^p$ norm and in local capacity while their measures $(\ddc u_j)^n$ tend vaguely to $c\delta_a$, for any $c>0$ and interior point $a$ (Book, Proposition~1.6.3, printed p.~25; the point-mass case of \cite[v1, Corollary 3.6, p.~14]{QinLimits26}). A common local bound would force the limit measure at the zero potential to vanish, by Book, Lemma~1.6.6. This bounded-domain construction is distinct from the fixed global Hermitian-background sequence displayed in S01 and does not prescribe its defect measure. More generally, for every bounded psh background $b$ on such a domain and every positive Radon measure $\nu$, there are bounded $u_j\leq b$ tending to $b$ in all finite $L^p$ norms and in local capacity, with $(\ddc u_j)^n\to(\ddc b)^n+\nu$ vaguely (Book, Theorem~1.6.4, printed p.~29; \cite[v1, Theorem B, p.~3]{QinLimits26}). The measure may have infinite total mass. The book gives smooth approximants when $b$ is smooth and proves the addition by lower-degree trace control and finite atomic iteration; this still does not prescribe the fixed global defect in S01. At the zero background, every vaguely closed subset of the positive Radon measures is the full vague cluster set of a sequence of smooth bounded negative psh functions tending to zero in every finite $L^p$ norm and in local capacity, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb C^n$, $n\geq2$ (Book, Theorem~1.6.5, printed p.~31; the zero-potential case of \cite[v1, Theorem A, pp.~2--3]{QinLimits26}). The empty cluster set is allowed. A vague metric transfers corresponding subsequential limits without assuming that moving target measures have uniformly bounded local masses; it does not imply convergence of their difference on every continuous compactly supported test (Book, Lemma~1.6.11 and the following counterexample, printed pp.~30--31). For a fixed bounded psh background $b$, the full vague cluster sets of bounded approximants $u_j\leq b$ tending to $b$ in all finite $L^p$ norms and in local capacity are exactly the vaguely closed sets all of whose members dominate $(\ddc b)^n$ (Book, Lemma~1.6.12 and Theorem~1.6.6, printed pp.~32--33). The empty set remains allowed, and the book gives smooth approximants for smooth $b$. The measure lower bound uses the capacity convergence in this regime; it is distinct from the source's general $L^1$ reachable-set classification. This full-cluster-set conclusion is local and leaves the fixed global S01 defect question open.\par The global smooth shrinking construction now has additional necessary restrictions (Book, Proposition~7.5.1, printed p.~173). For $H_j=\ddc w_j+s_j\omega\geq0$, every subsequential limit $K_k$ of $H_j^k$ is positive and closed, pairs to zero with every smooth complementary $\mathrm d$-closed or $\ddc$-closed form, and satisfies $K_1=K_n=0$. The defect is $\sum_{k=2}^{n-1}\binom nk\omega^{n-k}\wedge K_k$. A global closed semipositive form confines its support to that form's degeneracy set. There is no such excess in dimensions at most two, or on a threefold carrying a pluriclosed Hermitian metric. This statement uses global test forms and does not infer a restriction from a merely local K\"ahler form.\par On the standard Hopf threefold $X=(\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\})/\langle z\mapsto\mathrm e^{-1}z\rangle$, Book, Theorem~8.7.1, printed p.~194 gives a complete classification: for $b>6$, all defects are $\mathcal L\mu$, the Haar-probability fiber lifts of arbitrary positive measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb P^2$ of mass $b-6$. Every one is realized by normalized smooth $w_j=r_jU_j$ with exact mass $b$ and $0<r_j<\varepsilon_j$ for any prescribed bounds $\varepsilon_j\to0$. Their supports are precisely saturated supports $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\mu)$, with every nonempty closed saturated set realizable; they have no point atoms. They charge no pluripolar sets exactly when $\mu$ charges no base pluripolar sets. Smooth full-support defects, a full defect supported on one globally pluripolar fiber, and full-support defects assigning any fraction strictly between zero and one to a polar fiber all occur. The positive quadratic estimate (Book, Lemma~8.7.1, printed p.~190), orbital mixture construction for every probability law, including singular laws (Book, Proposition~8.7.1, printed p.~191), full intermediate-tensor necessity (Book, Lemma~8.7.2, printed p.~192), and repaired projective automorphisms (Book, Lemma~8.7.3, printed p.~193) prove full continuous-test convergence while retaining positivity and exact total mass.\par For every Hermitian metric $\Omega$ on this same Hopf threefold, Book, Theorem~8.7.2, printed p.~195 classifies the defects as $\mathcal L_\Omega\mu$ with mass $\mu(\mathbb P^2)=b-\int_X\Omega^3$. The fiber probability is $\Omega|_{\pi^{-1}(p)}/\int_{\pi^{-1}(p)}\Omega$, which need not be Haar. Supports, absence of point atoms, and the pluripolar equivalence are unchanged. The prescribed-mass correction solves the actual quadratic mass polynomial, including its linear term. Thus the entire metric family is settled, while general manifolds remain outside this classification.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine sufficient realization conditions on a general compact Hermitian manifold for positive closed intermediate currents with the stated vanishing pairings, and classify the resulting supports and pluripolar charging behaviors. The displayed shrinking smooth construction on the standard Hopf threefold is completely classified for every Hermitian metric, but the necessary current restrictions alone do not prove sufficiency on other manifolds.

supplemental_entries.title: Optimal damping on the Hopf BMP counterexample
supplemental_entries.statement: For the standard Hermitian Hopf threefold, determine the optimal decay conditions on a decreasing weight $W(t)$ ensuring finite weighted measures $W(-u)\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_\omega(u)$ for all normalized $u\leq0$, with uniform tail and capacity-continuity bounds.
supplemental_entries.state:
BMP fails on this threefold, while $v_-(\omega)=6$. The general damping theorem gives these conclusions for
\[W(t)=(1+t)^{-1}[\log(\mathrm e+t)]^{-a},\qquad a>1.\]
Exponential damping and stronger decay are available. The upper-mass counterexample is from Xia--Zhang \cite{XZ26}.
supplemental_entries.gap: Establish sharpness or improve the logarithmic factor, separating universal finiteness, uniform tails and capacity continuity if their thresholds differ. The critical power estimate is known; the optimal rate remains undetermined in the manuscript.

supplemental_entries.title: Exponential solvability when the individual threshold is zero
supplemental_entries.statement:
Let $v_-(h)=0$, let $f\geq0$ be a nonzero $L^1$ density with $b_h(f)=0$, and fix $\lambda>0$. Characterize when a genuine $s\in\PSH(X,h)$ satisfies
\[\mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_h(s)\geq\mathrm e^{\lambda s}f\,\mathrm dV,\]
and hence when the greatest finite-mass exponential solution exists. In particular, test the obstructing concentration density constructed in the lower-mass chapter.
supplemental_entries.state: Positive threshold supplies an exponential subsolution for every exponent. Any exponential subsolution gives a greatest exact solution by decreasing bounded-density approximation. The concentration example excludes all positive scaled subsolutions and therefore all bounded exponential solutions, but its argument does not exclude unbounded exponential solutions.
supplemental_entries.gap: Decide whether an unbounded potential can absorb the concentration through its exponential weight and find an intrinsic criterion at $b_h(f)=0$. This is distinct from P07, which assumes positive individual threshold.

supplemental_entries.title: Order-continuity of the density-root space at zero lower mass
supplemental_entries.statement: Write $\rho_h(p)=b_h(|p|^n)^{-1/n}$, $\mathcal D_h=\{p\in L^n:\rho_h(p)<\infty\}$, and let $\mathcal D_h^0$ be the closure of bounded roots in $\|p\|_{L^n}+\rho_h(p)$. If $v_-(h)=0$, is $\mathcal D_h^0=\mathcal D_h$? Separately, do uniform root tails suffice for the exact equation in P07?
supplemental_entries.state:
The manuscript proves
\[p\in\mathcal D_h^0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \rho_h(|p|\mathbf1_{\{|p|>K\}})\to0.\]
This is equivalent to norm convergence under all dominated perturbations tending to zero in measure. Smooth functions are dense in $\mathcal D_h^0$, which contains $L^r$ for $r>n$. If lower mass is positive, both spaces equal $L^n$. Root tails give scalar continuity, dual attainment and error moduli for exponential approximations.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine whether positive-threshold roots can have nonvanishing uniform tails. Even equality of the spaces would not automatically prove capacity convergence of equation potentials; that further implication needs a compactness argument.

supplemental_entries.title: Canonical selection and whole-family convergence at exponent zero
supplemental_entries.statement: For greatest positive-exponent solutions with fixed density and prescribed reference, determine conditions under which the normalized potentials converge to one canonical zero-exponent solution as $\lambda\downarrow0$. Extend the question to varying model references and densities while retaining their limiting type.
supplemental_entries.state: Under suitable lower-mass or model-volume hypotheses, scalars and equation measures converge; each normalized cluster limit solves the zero-exponent equation. Smooth and specified semipositive dual maximizers give uniqueness and whole-family convergence. The symmetric projective example has an explicitly selected limit. General Hermitian zero-exponent potentials need not be unique: smooth, quadratic-zero and real-analytic-density counterexamples are constructed.
supplemental_entries.gap: A general selection requires more than uniqueness of the scalar. Prove uniqueness of the selected limit or provide a robust variational or order characterization, particularly for $L^1$ data. Separate selection from the disproved assertion that all normalized solutions are unique. Related targets are P07 and S16.

supplemental_entries.title: Regularity for arbitrary prescribed types and at density zeros
supplemental_entries.statement: Find regularity and stability criteria for solutions in arbitrary prescribed ordinary or envelope types on a smooth big, possibly nonclosed background, beyond the resolved logarithmic and exceptional minimal types. At a density zero, identify conditions on the density and residual geometry that imply a smooth or H\"older residual, and state whether the conclusion extends across the singular set. Also obtain regularity criteria for general singular envelopes and weighted extremals beyond the stated density-in-capacity regimes.
supplemental_entries.state: The manuscript gives local continuity above a locally bounded strict barrier, local H\"older control for minimal $L^p$ solutions, and interior smoothness on the full regular locus of a fixed analytic strict barrier with smooth positive density. Resolved logarithmic types with positive residual and exceptional blowups have quantified H\"older remainders. Smooth positive global volume forms give ample-locus smoothness in every closed big K\"ahler class. On a smaller smooth-density open set there are compact examples of discontinuous bounded solutions. Smooth density zeros and their necessary vanishing order do not suffice for a smooth Hessian. Weighted extremals have regularity in specified uniform density-in-capacity regimes, which do not cover every singular envelope.
supplemental_entries.gap: Find sufficient type-sensitive hypotheses covering the remaining cases. Local density smoothness alone and determinant vanishing order alone are already insufficient. Regularity across the pole set must be justified separately from regularity on its complement.

supplemental_entries.title: Weak adjoints for singular references and a weak linearized equation
supplemental_entries.statement:
In every admissible singular-reference or degenerate-background regime of the normalization functional, determine when $\mathcal A_\varphi(F)$ is a singleton and when its probability is an approximation-independent adjoint of a weak linearized Monge--Amp\`ere operator. Specify a meaningful product and weight for
\[\ddc\bigl(\rho(\theta+\ddc u)^{n-1}\bigr)=0.\]
supplemental_entries.state:
Supporting probabilities and their stability are constructed without declaring this product defined. Generic uniqueness holds on a dense $G_\delta$ for each fixed admissible reference. Smooth potentials have the classical adjoint. If every smooth positive potential perturbation is Gauduchon, normalized Monge--Amp\`ere measures extend bounded adjoints and are continuous under bounded capacity convergence; this includes Gauduchon surfaces.
 Lemma 14.2.1, printed p.~450, gives an admissible ordinary divisorial model on $\mathbb P^1	imes\mathbb P^1$. With normalized pulled Fubini--Study forms, $	heta=2\omega_1+2\omega_2$, $ eta=\omega_1+2\omega_2$, $\mathrm dV=\omega_1\wedge\omega_2$ and $\psi=\log(|z|^2/(1+|z|^2))$, Proposition 14.2.3, printed p.~451, proves that every bounded-equivalent representative has non-pluripolar mass four, the sole support at $F=0$ is $\mathrm dV$, and the residual adjoint cofactor is $ eta/4$. Theorem 14.2.4, printed p.~452, constructs monotone uniformly positive smoothings $u_{\delta,g}=\log(r+\delta\mathrm e^g)$, where $r=|z|^2/(1+|z|^2)$ and $g$ is smooth on the second factor with $\ddc g\geq-\omega_2$. They converge canonically, in capacity and smoothly off $D=\{0\}	imes\mathbb P^1$, with $F_{\delta,g}=\log((	heta+\ddc u_{\delta,g})^2/(4\mathrm dV))	o0$ in every finite $L^p$. Yet their classical adjoint probabilities tend to $	frac12\mathrm dV+	frac12[D]\wedge\omega_2+	frac18[D]\wedge\ddc g$, which depends on $g$ and has divisor mass one half. Smooth mass eight differs from relative mass four, and the exponential densities fail uniform integrability. Section 33.10, printed p.~1152, explains the exact bounded-product, extension and integration premises.
 Corollary 14.2.1, printed p.~455, proves recovery in this fixed divisor type when $w_j,w\in\operatorname{PSH}(X, eta)$ have one common bound $|w_j|,|w|\leq M$ and $w_j	o w$ in capacity. The residual cofactors $Q_j=( eta+\ddc w_j)/4$ converge as currents and the residual probabilities $
u_j=( eta+\ddc w_j)^2/4$ converge weakly. The estimate in equation 14.9, printed p.~455, gives the quantitative bound $|\int f(\mathrm d
u_j-\mathrm d
u)|\leq C_f(2\eta+2M^2\operatorname{Cap}_ eta\{|w_j-w|>\eta\})$ when $-C_f eta\leq\ddc f\leq C_f eta$. When the residual forms are smooth and strictly positive these are their classical adjoints; the canonical singular potentials retain the same divisor. At a continuous relative solution the limiting probability is the sole supporting probability.
supplemental_entries.gap: Unrestricted smooth recovery fails even for this admissible reference with singleton support and a defined residual adjoint. The fixed divisor and uniformly bounded residual capacity-convergence regime is established above. Recovery for more general singular references, unbounded residual sequences or varying conformal multipliers remains open, as does the construction of an approximation-independent weak operator in the general singular-reference or degenerate-background regime. The positive result is conditional on the stated residual approximation; it does not assert that every bounded residual has such a smooth approximation. P16 asks the narrower singleton question for a Hermitian background and nonsingular reference; neither this concentration example nor this fixed-divisor result resolves it.

supplemental_entries.title: Continuity when singular references or positive residuals degenerate
supplemental_entries.statement: Give geometric or singularity conditions on varying admissible references $\varphi_j$ and backgrounds that imply convergence of $B_{\varphi_j}$ on continuous tests and place all cluster supports in $\mathcal A_\varphi(F)$ for the limiting reference. Include degenerate residual forms and arbitrary singularities.
supplemental_entries.state: A genuine smaller-background envelope tending to reference zero gives uniform convergence of scalar functionals and uniformly integrable supports. Relative comparison of positive divisorial residuals gives a geometric criterion. Entropy estimates yield compactness while references vary. BMP model-volume and fixed-divisor regimes supply additional equation stability. For closed projective backgrounds and one fixed point blowup, Theorem~14.11.1, printed p.~476, proves uniform convergence on all continuous tests from Hausdorff convergence of convex bodies containing one common translated simplex and positive scales tending to a positive limit. The actual limiting ordinary model has positive mass and is independently solvable for every bounded Borel test; supporting probabilities are the normalized exponential densities. Proposition~14.11.1, printed p.~477, and Corollary~14.11.1, printed p.~478, give a varying nonanalytic isolated-pole family with positive limiting mass. Proposition~14.11.2, printed p.~479, and Corollary~14.11.2, printed p.~479, give smooth residuals that have rank one on an exceptional divisor but positive top mass; the zero-mass endpoint is excluded for every bounded ordinary-type remainder.
supplemental_entries.gap: The common-simplex criterion settles these closed projective and fixed-blowup families, including the two stated degenerations. Extend it to nonclosed Hermitian backgrounds, moving modifications or unrestricted singularity degeneration. Compactness of measures alone does not identify their supporting functional; limiting-reference solvability must be established. These results do not assert convergence of solution potentials or define rough weighted adjoint products.

supplemental_entries.title: Zero-obstacle equality versus equality at every obstacle
supplemental_entries.statement:
For an admissible smooth background $\theta$ and $u\in\PSH(X,\theta)$, does
\[P_\theta[u]=P_\theta[u]_{\mathcal I}\]
imply $P_{\theta,F}[u]=P_{\theta,F}[u]_{\mathcal I}$ for every smooth real obstacle $F$, without positive lower ideal volume or BMP?
supplemental_entries.state: All-obstacle equality always implies zero-obstacle equality. The converse follows from membership in the relative envelope class of the ideal envelope. Under BMP and positive lower ideal volume it is a theorem; on curves it holds without volume restrictions. It also holds on specified separated products, auxiliary products without ambient BMP, and divisorial curve fibrations with the stated descent hypotheses. All-obstacle uniformity is smooth-gauge invariant.
supplemental_entries.gap: Establish the converse in unrestricted higher-dimensional zero-volume and unbounded-mass settings or give a counterexample. The positive-volume criterion cannot be applied at lower volume zero. This is an explicit subproblem overlapping P06 and the analytic-closure part of P01/P17.

supplemental_entries.title: Perron interpolation and a metric geometry of singularity classes
supplemental_entries.statement: Relate Hermitian Perron segments and their Legendre-dual test curves to geodesics for a complete metric on singularity classes. Identify hypotheses under which this interpolation is stationary for a specified action and compatible with a complete singularity topology.
supplemental_entries.state: The minimum principle and Legendre duality give Perron interpolation without a closed background. For the raw $L^2$ action, the Euler equation has torsion terms. A primitive for the raw Monge--Amp\`ere one-form near zero forces closedness. On a Gauduchon three-torus, a smooth Perron segment need not be stationary; on surfaces the Gauduchon condition persists but does not remove the first-derivative terms.
supplemental_entries.gap: Specify a metric/action whose geometry fits the interpolation, rather than importing the K\"ahler energy primitive. The raw-primitive obstruction and nonstationary example are settled; the remaining target is a coherent replacement compatible with P01/P17.

supplemental_entries.title: Nonclosed restricted positivity and its relation to intrinsic traces
supplemental_entries.statement: Construct a restricted positivity invariant for general nonclosed backgrounds and relate it to intrinsic multiplier-ideal trace data. Determine when positive residual or restricted mass produces a strict current of a specified one-sided or ordinary singularity type.
supplemental_entries.state: For closed classes on class-$\mathcal C$ manifolds, a finite resolution-independent restricted invariant is positive exactly when the resolved class is big; for nef classes its zero union is the null locus. For divisorial traces with bounded remainder, a mass polynomial and residual comparison produce strict currents more singular than the trace. Preserving bounded-difference type can fail even on a projective surface.
supplemental_entries.gap: Extend the invariant beyond the closed or bounded-residual regimes and separate one-sided domination from preservation of ordinary type. Universal equality of restricted mass and ambient positive-product data is contradicted by the trace examples. This connects P06, P18 and P14.

supplemental_entries.title: Inverse realization of divisors at a global or prescribed-type threshold
supplemental_entries.statement: Given an effective real divisor $E$ and the annihilating face of normalized Gauduchon tests associated to its Bott--Chern class, determine when a threshold subsolution for $f$ has $\omega+\ddc u\geq[E]$. Separately formulate and characterize the maximal coefficient among potentials in one prescribed singularity type.
supplemental_entries.state:
If a coefficient-$c$ subsolution contains $[E]$, the manuscript proves
\[c\leq b_\omega(f)(1-\kappa_\omega(\beta_E))^n,\]
where $\beta_E$ represents $\{E\}$ and $\kappa_\omega$ is its linear positivity threshold. At $c=b_\omega(f)$, every smooth maximizing sequence annihilates $\beta_E$ in the limit; uniform integrability ensures its cluster current maximizes the dual functional. The corresponding exposed face lies in the weak closure of smooth tests.
supplemental_entries.gap: Determine sufficient conditions converting annihilation into an actual divisorial component. Do not assume all Gauduchon currents are smoothly approximable, or define $[E]\wedge T$ for a singular test merely by its smooth class pairing. A global threshold need not equal a threshold restricted to one type.

supplemental_entries.title: Completeness under nefness and geometric smoothing compatibility
supplemental_entries.statement: For a divisorial exponential equation in a nef big class, or for data satisfying the geometric smoothing compatibility conditions of \cite[Section 3.1]{DNGL26}, determine whether its positive metric on the regular locus is complete. In the smoothing problem, retain the prescribed nonintegrable divisor pole with coefficient smooth and strictly positive across the divisor.
supplemental_entries.state: Both original completeness assertions have negative answers. Book, Theorem~27.14.2, printed p.~941 gives a semipositive nef and big background on the blowup of $\mathbb P^2$, with a unique full-mass finite-energy solution, zero Lelong numbers and the prescribed nonintegrable pole with smooth strictly positive coefficient. Its cusp is complete, but a disjoint null exceptional curve is at finite distance. Book, Theorem~27.14.3, printed p.~946 gives an incomplete auxiliary solution for exact geometric smoothing data on the blowup of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. The initial residual is K\"ahler, the original volume is fixed as $\omega^2$, and the resolution, discrepancy and residual-volume identities hold exactly. Its auxiliary class is non-nef. The minimal reference has a divisorial logarithm; the solution adds a zero-Lelong cusp and has finite relative energy. Every dense Zariski open positive regular locus is incomplete in both examples. The earlier non-nef example has an ordinary minimal solution; H\"older residuals and logarithmically weakened torus poles supply further normal-length tests.
supplemental_entries.gap: The original question is settled for its two separate regimes. Further refinements are completeness under simultaneous nefness and exact smoothing compatibility, and completeness for an actual evolving maximal flow. The compatible elliptic example has a non-nef class; the nef example chooses its smooth volume as part of the construction. Neither identifies its auxiliary solution with an evolving flow metric. Smooth local convergence requested in P12 also does not establish completeness.
supplemental_entries.status: resolved in original two separate regimes; joint and evolving-flow refinements open

supplemental_entries.title: Higher-dimensional growing-jet limits and transfer through fibrations
supplemental_entries.statement: Formulate and prove higher-dimensional analogues of the growing-jet transition in P22, and criteria transferring such local limits through Hermitian fibrations. Specify the vanishing ideal, local curvature degeneracy, moving observation scale, Hilbert norm, and intrinsic section-growth normalization.
supplemental_entries.state:
A precise compact sufficient-condition class is proved in Section~26.15, printed p.~880. Let $Y=(\mathbb P^1)^q$, $q\geq2$, $L=\boxtimes_j\mathcal O(r_j+1)$, with unequal integers $r_j\geq2$ and $\varepsilon_j>0$. In the affine frame use $\phi=\sum_j\log(1+|z_j|^{2r_j}+\varepsilon_j|z_j|^{2r_j+2})$ and the smooth volume $\nu_Y=\prod_j(1+|z_j|^2)^{-2}\mathrm dA_j$, of total mass $\pi^q$. For ordinary point jets $V_m=H^0(Y,L^m\otimes\mathfrak m_x^{k_m})$, $k_m\to\infty$, $k_m=o(m)$, put $t_j=|z_j|^2$, $\psi_j(t)=\log(1+t^{r_j}+\varepsilon_jt^{r_j+1})$, $H_j=t\psi_j'$, $G_j=tH_j'$ and $g_j=G_j/t$. If $mH_j(t_j)/k_m\to\alpha_j>0$, $\sum_j\alpha_j=1$, and $(\sum_jmH_j(t_j)-k_m)/\sqrt{\sum_jmG_j(t_j)}\to\tau$, then
\[
 \frac{\pi^q a(t)B_m(z)}{m^q\prod_jg_j(t_j)}\longrightarrow\Phi(\tau),
 \qquad a(t)=\prod_j(1+t_j)^{-2}.
\]
This includes every sublinear order with the actual radial center. Exact global monomials give $\dim V_m=\prod_j((r_j+1)m+1)-\binom{k_m+q-1}{q}$ and $m^{-q}B_m\nu_Y\to c_1(L,h)^q/q!$ in total variation (Book, Theorem~26.15.1, printed p.~881). The homogeneous center has the sharp smaller range $k_m=o(m^{2/(r_*+2)})$, $r_*:=\max_jr_j$; positive first remainders produce a nonzero critical Gaussian shift and supercritical limit one (Book, Proposition~26.15.1, printed p.~883).

For a compact holomorphic submersion $\pi:X\to Y$ with connected fibers of dimension $f\geq1$, a pullback bundle and metric and a matched smooth volume $\pi_*\nu_X=\nu_Y$, the moving isolated selector $\varphi_m=(k_m+q+f-1)\chi_p/m$ has $\mathcal I(m\varphi_m)=\mathfrak m_p^{k_m}$. Its pole and ideal do not descend, but selected sections and their smooth norms identify exactly with $V_m$. Thus $B_{X,m}=B_m\circ\pi$, the growth exponent is $q$, and the lifted density converges in total variation. Matched volumes exist on every such submersion; arbitrary volumes instead transform the base norm, for which this local theorem has not been proved (Book, Theorem~26.15.2, printed p.~884). This moving selector does not close the fixed-selector problem P21.

At a fixed zero of curvature, an explicit smooth semipositive metric on $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}(1)$ already gives the unselected kernel scale $B_m(p)=3m/(\pi^2\rho_0\log m)(1+O((\log m)^{-1}))$ for a smooth positive two-torus-invariant probability volume with local density $\rho_0$ (Book, Proposition~26.14.1, printed p.~879). The leading constant is $3/2$ for Fubini--Study probability volume. The metric is the exact model of \cite[Example I.15, pp.~9--10]{ChiangKernel26}; the manuscript proves the norm asymptotic directly by elementary integrals. No growing vanishing ideal or moving-scale limit is included in this example.
supplemental_entries.gap: Extend beyond the specified separable radial class: mixed or angular remainders, observation faces with some zero energy fractions, other compact bases or ideals, and general fiber-selected singularities. Control global section production and the transformed norm at the moving scale in each new regime. The proved sufficient conditions do not imply a universal Gaussian expression or an ambient-dimensional Monge--Amp\`ere limit.

supplemental_entries.title: Individual solvability criteria for arbitrary non-pluripolar measures
supplemental_entries.statement: Extend the individual-density threshold criterion from $f\,\mathrm dV$ to a fixed finite nonzero non-pluripolar Borel measure $\nu$. Find an intrinsic criterion for a positive scaled subsolution, an exact normalized equation, and an exponential equation, distinguishing these three assertions.
supplemental_entries.state: Positive lower mass characterizes solvability for every finite non-pluripolar measure. Prescribed-reference versions have their explicit model and lower-volume assumptions. At zero lower mass some absolutely continuous probability measures already admit no positive scaled subsolution, while smooth densities remain solvable. For individual densities, bounded truncations and the Gauduchon root formula give an exact subsolution criterion.
supplemental_entries.gap: For a general $\nu$, there is no canonical bounded-density truncation relative to smooth volume. Replace this construction while retaining measure domination and finite-mass compactness. This extends P07/S03 and is not implied by solving all smooth densities.

supplemental_entries.title: Automatic envelope genuineness in semipositive dual attainment
supplemental_entries.statement: Suppose a positive-threshold $L^1$ density has a smooth semipositive maximizing Gauduchon current, strictly positive off a proper analytic set $Z$, and let $\Phi_f$ be the greatest normalized threshold subsolution. Find conditions making $P_{\delta h}(\Phi_f)$ genuine for some $0<\delta<1$, and determine regularity across $Z$. More generally, ask whether moment or entropy control forces this envelope condition.
supplemental_entries.state: The semipositive maximizer gives a unique exact global threshold solution, smoothness off $Z$, a fixed lower barrier and whole-family normalized $L^1$ convergence of exponential solutions. A genuine smaller-background envelope upgrades to capacity convergence; $L^p$ data, $p>1$, give continuity and uniform convergence. For rough maximizing currents, first moments plus this envelope condition yield an exact cluster equation. Entropy bounds supply moments and uniform integrability but do not supply the envelope.
supplemental_entries.gap: Prove automatic genuineness under additional intrinsic assumptions or identify its failure, and separate regularity across $Z$ from off-$Z$ smoothness. These are stronger compactness and regularity questions than exact solvability in the already settled semipositive regime.

supplemental_entries.title: Critical determinant bounds restricted to actual adjoint maximizers
supplemental_entries.statement: When $v_-(h)=0$, determine whether the critical $L^{n/(n-1)}$ estimate can hold for the determinant-weighted probabilities of exact maximizing currents representing adjoints, uniformly as $F$ ranges over a specified bounded set. Identify geometric or density hypotheses for such a restricted estimate.
supplemental_entries.state:
All normalized Gauduchon tests can violate the endpoint, while their subcritical estimates hold universally. Adjoint densities inherit those subcritical bounds; positive lower mass supplies the endpoint. For one fixed smooth strictly positive density the exact maximizer is smooth and unique. Near-maximizing sequences can have divergent higher moments even on K"ahler manifolds.
 Theorem 25.8.3, printed p.~710, now gives uniform $L^\infty$ bounds for both $k_{T_F}$ and $q_F=\mathrm d
u_F/\mathrm dV$ on every fixed smooth positive background of dimension $n\geq3$, including $v_-(h)=0$, for a fixed $0<\alpha<1$, a smooth positive probability volume $\mathrm dV$, and smooth $F$ in an explicit small $C^{2,\alpha}$ ball around $\log(h^n/(V_h\mathrm dV))$. Lemma 25.8.1, printed p.~709, gives the two controlled solution and factor constructions; Corollary 25.8.2, printed p.~711, gives probability-normalized families of arbitrary finite dimension and a path of distinct data and exact currents. The exact bounds are $C_
u=3^{n+1}aH_{\max}/4$ and $C_k=3^naH_{\max}^{(n-1)/n}/2$, where $\int\chi_0h^n=1$, $a=\max\chi_0$ and $H_{\max}=\max(h^n/\mathrm dV)$; at the critical exponent, the probability norm is at most $C_
u^{1/n}$. Primary elliptic locators are explained in Section 33.13, printed p.~1155.
supplemental_entries.gap: The small smooth $C^{2,\alpha}$ family supplies one sufficient density hypothesis. Endpoint bounds for larger families or for merely continuous densities bounded in $C^0$ or $L^\infty$ remain open. The theorem concerns exact maximizers; it gives no uniform higher-moment bound for all tests or near-maximizers. Keep $k_T$ separate from the normalized $F$-weighted probability density. It does not resolve P16 at arbitrary continuous data.

supplemental_entries.title: Moving positive products and birational volume formulas for nonclosed data
supplemental_entries.statement: Develop a nonclosed analogue of moving intersection or birational volume data that records imposed poles and residual positivity, and relate it to the Gauduchon subtraction cost of P14. Specify the invariant and its gauge and modification behavior before asserting a volume formula.
supplemental_entries.state: Finite divisor residuals have explicit mass polynomials and Gauduchon variation formulas. Closed class-$\mathcal C$ restricted invariants are resolution independent; closed K\"ahler positive products and volume differentiability are literature inputs. For nonclosed nef backgrounds, irrational or oscillatory volume orders and modification jumps obstruct direct transfer of the closed numerical formulas.
supplemental_entries.gap: This is a stated research objective, rather than a fully formulated conjecture in the manuscript. A solution needs a precise construction accounting for differential background data and the distinction between upper singularity volume and fixed-density variational volume.

supplemental_entries.title: Optimal multiweight ideal distance when the number of weights exceeds the dimension
supplemental_entries.statement:
Fix integers $n\geq2$, $r>n$, and real exponents $p_1,\ldots,p_r>1$. Determine the smallest universal constant $C(n;p_1,\ldots,p_r)$ such that the following inequality holds on every pseudoconvex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n$: for genuine psh $\psi$, genuine negative psh $\phi_i$, and holomorphic $f$ with $0<I=\int_\Omega|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi-\sum_i\phi_i}\,\mathrm dV<+\infty$,
\[
 \inf\left\{\int_\Omega|g|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi}\,\mathrm dV:
       g\in\mathcal O(\Omega),\quad
       f-g\in\sum_{i=1}^r\Gamma(\Omega,\mathcal I(p_i\phi_i+\psi))\right\}
       \leq C(n;p_1,\ldots,p_r)I.
\]
Global ideal membership means local integrability at every germ; it does not require a finite global norm for the subtracted sections. Establish both the universal upper estimate and examples attaining it or approaching it.
supplemental_entries.state:
Book Theorem~1.16.2, printed p.~63, proves the upper constant $\prod_i(1-1/p_i)$ for every $r$, with equality models when $r\leq n$. Theorem~1.16.3, printed pp.~66--67, determines the optimal constant $\max\{1-\sum_i1/p_i,0\}$ for every $r$ in dimension one; when the reciprocal sum is at least one, $g=0$ is admissible. Takakura's exact preprint \cite[v1, Theorem~1.2 and Example~3.2, pp.~1--2 and 7]{TakDivision26} states the dimension-dependent bound $1-\frac{\sum_i1/p_i}{\min\{n,r\}}$ under $\sum_i1/p_i<\min\{n,r\}$ and asks about optimality. Its general higher-rank proof is not an adopted input of the manuscript; the book reconstructs scalar division and the stated product and planar estimates directly.
Book Example~1.16.1, printed pp.~67--68, constructs unit-ball hyperplane weights with equal exponents $p$, for every $n\geq2$, $r>n$ and $r/n<p\leq r$. The reciprocal sum is in $[1,n)$, the input integral is finite, and the distance equals $\pi^n/n!>0$. It gives a positive lower bound $\pi^n/(n!I)$ for the corresponding universal constant and excludes extending the planar zero regime to higher dimensions. It does not determine the optimal constant.
supplemental_entries.gap: For $n\geq2$ and $r>n$, the known product estimate has no equality argument using $r$ distinct coordinate directions. Determine how the common zero sets and the interaction of multiplier ideals affect the optimal constant. The planar principal-ideal calculation does not extend to arbitrary higher-dimensional ideals. This is a local quantitative problem, distinct from global $\mathcal I$-goodness in P01/P06.
